Hi Irene,

Thanks for making time for the assessor intake. To keep our review scope narrow we asked for a compact SDLC appendix that covers: code review process (PR gating + sampling), CI/CD controls (pipeline stages and artifact provenance), secrets handling (ephemeral tokens, KMS integration), and change management (approval matrix and commit trace).

Can you provide a single-folder delivery (index file + representative artifacts) that we can ingest? If possible we prefer short artifacts (CSV manifests, redacted pipeline logs, and a short narrative) rather than a bulk zip.

Timeline: we need submission by EOD 2026-05-07 to meet the assessment window.

Best,
Morgan

Morgan — forwarding the artifact set for the compact appendix. Files uploaded to the Drive folder and linked in the index. Highlights and redactions provided below.

Attached artifacts (representative):
- ci-pipeline-run-2026-04-28.pdf (pipeline stage timing, artifact checksums; commit IDs partially redacted for customer privacy)
- pr-review-sampling-2026.csv (last 90 days; reviewer count, approval times, labels)
- ephemeral-kms-rotation-log.txt (rotation timestamps and key IDs; HSM-backed entries noted)
- sdlc-evidence-index.csv (manifest mapping artifacts to control statements)

Key clarifications:
- We enforce required approvers on release branches and use a two-person rule for production deploys. PR sampling shows 87% compliance with required approvers and an average time-to-merge of 3.2 hours.
- CI pipeline includes artifact signing step (internal sig), SBOM generation for release artifacts, and a provenance record with SHA256 checksums.
- Secrets: build agents use ephemeral tokens issued by our internal token broker; tokens expire at 15 minutes. Persistent secrets are stored in a KMS with automatic rotation every 90 days for service keys.
- Change mgmt: we keep an approval matrix in Confluence and link each release to a JIRA ticket; included three example traces in the Drive (release-trace-1/2/3).

Let us know if you want unredacted commit hashes for forensic review — we can provide under an NDA/secure channel.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we close the intake:

1) Ephemeral tokens — can you confirm which services issue them (internal broker vs. cloud provider)? Also, how are agent credentials scoped?
2) PR gating exceptions — do you have an audit trail for exception approvals (who approved, rationale)? The sampling CSV shows a small number of bypasses.
3) Artifact provenance — can you confirm the SBOM generator/tool and whether that SBOM is versioned with the artifact?

If you can answer in-line here and drop any short logs (redacted) it will speed review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Morgan
Assessment Team, AssessorCo
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Morgan Lee <morgan.lee@assessorco.com>, hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-05-07T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SDLC appendix artifacts (CI logs + PR sample) — clarifications

Morgan — quick answers inline: 

1) Ephemeral tokens: issued by our internal token broker (AuthMint). Agent credentials are scoped by role and service tag; broker mints short-lived bearer tokens tied to an agent ID. Cloud provider temp creds (IAM STS) are used only for cloud infra actions and are bound to the broker-issued principal.

2) PR gating exceptions: exceptions are requested via an internal Slack channel and recorded in the PR with a formal approval checklist. We keep an exceptions audit CSV (included in Drive: pr-exceptions-2026.csv) that contains approver, timestamp, and justification. Exceptions require a manager + security reviewer sign-off for production.

3) SBOM: we use Syft (anchored at version 0.85) invoked in the pipeline; SBOM JSON is stored alongside the artifact with a semantic version tag (artifact-vX.Y.Z-sbom.json). We also hash the SBOM into the artifact provenance record.

If you need the pr-exceptions CSV or SBOMs delivered directly rather than via Drive, we can provide them through the secure intake link or under a short NDA.

Happy to jump on a call if any of these need deeper context.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Release Platforms — Redwood Inference
